newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian Petrolexport denies report on pay troubles.
newsitem.headline: Romanian Petrolexport denies report on pay troubles.

text.p: Romania's main oil trader Petrolexportimport SA denied on Tuesday local media reports that lack of funds had prevented the National Oil Company (CRP) from making vital crude oil imports for the coming winter.

The private news agency Mediafax said a tanker laden with 130,000 tonnes of crude oil had been waiting since November 13 at the main oil terminal in the Black Sea port of Constanta because the CRP was unable to pay for the crude.
"The report is untrue. The tanker has discharged the crude and left Constanta three days ago," said an official from Petrolexport, which handles all major oil deals for CRP.
Oil terminal authorities in Constanta confirmed the Astra had sailed to Iran's Kharg Island in the Middle East Gulf on November 16 after discharging 130,000 tonnes of crude.

Mediafax said the alleged payment difficulties were related to a halt in talks between Chase Manhattan Corp and CRP on a $200 million revolving credit for crude imports. That followed a court ruling ordering the suspension of a July government decree to create the CRP.
"That's a different matter and it is for the competent authorities to decide," said the Petrolexport official, who asked not to be identified.

Last week, the Court of Appeal ordered the suspension of the CRP after a local private firm, General Trading and Investments Co SA (GTI), filed a lawsuit accusing the state-run holding of monopolistic practices.
The CRP has repeatedly denied GTI's charges and threatened to sue the company for libel and damages.
Chase Manhattan said it would continue talks on the loan and asked the CRP to clarify the suspension issue.

The Petrolexport official also denied Mediafax reports saying two other tankers expected by end-November, each carrying 70,000 tonnes of crude, might face problems. The report said the state Bancorex SA foreign trade bank had refused demands by CRP to issue letters of credit.

"Our general manager is now at Bancorex to get letters of credit for two shipments of crude expected next week and totalling 273,000 tonnes," the Petrolexport official said. -- Adrian Dascalu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
